_note: Reusable component recipes. Each lists structure + the key CSS/JS so the Programmer can build it consistently. Tag every visual with data-des for traceability.

hero_teaser.use: Opening full-viewport moment before the headline.
hero_teaser.build: Full-bleed container; background = generated image OR muted autoplay-loop video OR an interactive. Gradient scrim (transparent -> --bg) bottom 60% for text legibility. Headline + dek overlaid bottom-left in the content column. A small kicker (uppercase, letter-spaced) above the headline.
hero_teaser.rich_upgrade: Prefer a subtly animated hero (image2video parallax, or a CSS/canvas ambient motion) over a flat still when motion suits the subject.

hero_video.use: A muted autoplay-loop, full-bleed video as the opening hero — the most immersive hero option when the subject has motion.
hero_video.build: `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline poster=...>` full-bleed (100vw, object-fit:cover, behind the headline) + the same gradient scrim + headline overlay as hero_teaser. ALWAYS set muted + playsinline (mobile autoplay needs both) and a poster image (first-paint + reduced-motion fallback). Under prefers-reduced-motion, show the poster still instead of playing. Keep it short and seamless-looping.
hero_video.sourcing_decision_tree: (1) DEFAULT: license-clean stock loop (Pexels / Pixabay video) matching the subject; (2) AI-GENERATED generic action (text2video / image2video) when a GENERIC, publish-safe motion conveys the mood and no clean stock fits; (3) REAL footage (accept-IP) ONLY when a recognizable real moment is essential to the story — flag it for rip-out / replacement at the publish gate (see media_presentation license_posture).
hero_video.ab_toggle: When both exist, offer a real/AI A-B toggle so the AUTHOR (in the local build) can pick which hero reads best; the chosen-and-cleared one ships.
hero_video.anti_pattern: A YouTube `<iframe>` is NOT a seamless hero loop — it shows chrome, can't reliably autoplay-muted-from-zero, loops with a flash, and fails on file:// (Error 150/153). Use a real `<video>` element for a hero; reserve iframes for a captioned, click-to-play 'watch the clip' embed elsewhere.

stat_callout.single: Big numeral (var(--accent), weight 800, clamp ~2-3rem) + short label below; on a --surface panel with a left accent border for the marquee stat.
stat_callout.trio: flex row of 3 numerals with captions, under the headline, to set scale fast.
stat_callout.rule: Reserve stat callouts for the few most quotable numbers; don't turn every figure into one.

pull_quote: Oversized serif/italic quote, constrained width, accent rule or oversized quotation mark. For a striking sentence or a sourced quote.

card_deck.use: Many comparable items (locations, entities, products) the reader browses lightly — title + a photo + 1-2 stats each. For OWN auditable per-entity metrics (a scored profile), use entity_cards instead.
card_deck.build: Responsive VERTICAL grid (repeat(auto-fill, minmax(~240px,1fr))) — NOT a horizontal carousel (readers won't horizontally scroll; see interaction_playbook no_horizontal_scroll). Each card: image (real photo preferred) + title + 1-2 key stats. If a stepped horizontal paging genuinely suits a SMALL set (3-7), use the scroll_snap_stepper recipe (keyboard + dot rail), never a bare scroll-x row.
card_deck.rich_upgrade: Use real fetched photos (Wikimedia/press/Scout-verified) for concrete subjects rather than generic AI fills; a deck mixing real photos with silhouette placeholders looks unfinished — every card gets a real image or the deck is cut.

entity_cards.use: A deck profiling people / teams / items / locations with YOUR OWN auditable, normalized metrics (an EA-FC-style 0-99 rating card). The signature 'scored profile' deck — distinct from card_deck (which is a light browse).
entity_cards.build: VERTICAL responsive grid (repeat(auto-fill, minmax(~260px,1fr)); gap = design_tokens space_scale) with a sort/filter bar above (sort by any metric, filter by group) — NEVER a horizontal-scroll carousel. Each card top-to-bottom: real photo (every entity, no silhouettes) -> name + overall score (big numeral) + group/role -> a small RADAR/spider of the attributes -> the SAME attributes as a STACKED COLUMN of labeled bars DIRECTLY BELOW the radar (full card width each). Bars below, never beside, the radar — a side-by-side split starves the bars of width and they become unreadable.
entity_cards.metrics_rule: Metrics are the Analyst's OWN derived, documented, normalized-to-a-fixed-scale (e.g. 0-99) numbers from the data_table — never invented or copied from a game. Each card carries a provenance badge (data source + 'derived metric') and a 'sources ▾' disclosure (<details>) that expands the formula + raw inputs for every number, so each value is traceable.
entity_cards.polish: Apple-grade: pull radius (~14-16px), padding, gap and shadow from design_tokens (space_scale + soft shadow + consistent radius); hover-lift (translateY(-4px) + deepen shadow, transition var(--dur-md) var(--ease-out)); staggered MOT6-safe entrance (fade+rise, .delay(i*k), collapses to instant under prefers-reduced-motion). Card surface = --surface; numerals in --accent.
entity_cards.layout_rule: Radar ABOVE, attribute bars STACKED BELOW (one per row, full width). The cheap-looking failure is radar-left / bars-right. Tag every card data-des.
entity_cards.anti_pattern: Horizontal carousel; missing photos / silhouette fills; radar beside bars; un-sourced numbers; ratings borrowed from an actual game instead of derived from the data.

chart_frame: Chart in a block with margin:2rem auto AND text-align:center (so a chart narrower than the container — faceted/concat/step charts ignore width:container — centers instead of left-aligning; center the rendered SVG with `.vega-embed svg{display:block;margin:0 auto}` — NEVER set the .vega-embed wrapper to display:inline-block, which makes Vega measure 0 width and renders width:container charts invisible), a short caption (var(--muted)) and a source note. Style the chart to the theme tokens (axis colors, accent highlight) — never ship default Vega colors. On the always-on DARK cinematic stage, force LIGHT guide text: config.title.color AND config.title.subtitleColor (subtitleColor is a separate property — unset, the subtitle takes Vega's dark default and is invisible), plus config.axis.labelColor/titleColor and config.legend.labelColor/titleColor (use the dark `_config_block` in dataviz-craft/references/axis_label_polish.json) — PIT-62. Annotate the key datum directly.
map_frame: Leaflet with dark/muted tiles (e.g. CARTO dark/positron), custom circle markers colored by the shared data scale and sized by a second variable, popups in UI font, a small legend explaining color + size. Fixed height ~440-520px; disable scroll-wheel zoom to avoid scroll traps. For a marquee, immersive geographic centerpiece, use rich_map instead.

rich_map.use: An immersive geographic centerpiece — all locations as data-scaled markers, blended into the cinematic page rather than boxed.
rich_map.build: Leaflet, dark/muted tiles (CARTO dark/positron). Every location a marker SIZED and COLORED by a shared data scale (radius = scale(metricA); fill = scale(metricB)); a small legend explains both encodings. Rich popups: a real photo (Scout/Wikimedia-verified) + name + 2-3 key stats in UI font. HIGHLIGHT the marquee node(s) (a ring / larger radius / accent stroke / a permanent label) so the hero location reads instantly. On load, `map.fitBounds(L.featureGroup(markers).getBounds(), {padding:[40,40]})` so the data frames itself.
rich_map.presentation: Full-bleed (escape the content column, 100vw) with minimal or NO border / very subtle radius, so it blends into the cinematic background instead of sitting in a card. Generous height (~70-88vh for a centerpiece).
rich_map.scroll_trap_fix: Scroll-wheel zoom ONLY while the cursor is over the map: `map.scrollWheelZoom.disable(); map.on('mouseover',()=>map.scrollWheelZoom.enable()); map.on('mouseout',()=>map.scrollWheelZoom.disable());` — so wheeling past it never hijacks page scroll, but a deliberate hover lets the reader zoom. Keep dragPan on; tag data-des.
rich_map.rule: Never fake a map without real coordinates (see media_presentation). Tiles must be the allowed Leaflet CDN.

audio_player.sonification: A labeled 'play' button bound to a chart/timeline that lights up as it plays; Web Audio oscillators; never autoplay; visual fallback if muted.
audio_player.sound_design: The SFX / atmospheric sound-design form (a text2music/Lyria bed or any short reader-triggered cue) for a sound with NO findable real recording (a tension drone, a glass-shatter texture, a scene bed). Section-integrated mini-control (chapter break, scene overlay) with caption + a visible play/pause/<audio> control; event/section-triggered (IntersectionObserver), short, reader-controlled, never autoplay. NOT the front-of-blog BGM — the BGM is always a real sourced track in signature_media_card. (Legacy name: 'generated'.)
audio_player.embed: Native Spotify embed in a rounded, shadowed frame with a caption. For YouTube/video on a file:// page, prefer a click-through thumbnail FACADE (thumbnail https://img.youtube.com/vi/{ID}/hqdefault.jpg + play overlay, linking to the watch page in a new tab): a live YouTube iframe fails with a player 'configuration error' (Error 150/153) from a null file:// origin. Only embed a live YouTube iframe when the page is served over http(s). For an OFFICIAL anthem/theme song as the PRIMARY player, use signature_media_card — a 3rd-party embed must never be the primary player (non-logged-in users get a ~30s preview + no autoplay-from-start).

signature_media_card.use: The PRIMARY front-of-blog BGM player, MANDATORY on EVERY blog (no opt-out): a self-hosted player that lets the reader actually HEAR a REAL track, not just see a link. It sits at the TOP of the article, directly BELOW THE TITLE (in-flow, so the reader can't miss it), and its cover is a SPINNING VINYL DISC (see vinyl_cover). The BGM is ALWAYS a real sourced track — NEVER an AI-composed track (text2music is the opt-in sound-design/SFX form only, see audio_player.sound_design). When the story has no topic-fitting real track and no signature track, the guaranteed floor is a license-clean classical RECORDING (verify the recording's license, not just the composition's PD status); it still plays in this same player.

vinyl_cover.what: THE cover treatment on every blog — the album/track cover art rendered as a CIRCULAR DISC (a spinning vinyl) that rotates ONLY while playing. Upgrades the old static square cover; the player itself keeps its top-of-article, below-the-title placement.
vinyl_cover.structure: The cover art clipped to a CIRCLE (`border-radius:50%`, object-fit:cover) as a spinning vinyl disc + the track TITLE + the ARTIST(S) + a SINGLE play/pause button (>=44x44px) + (optional) a small status label. The disc replaces the square cover; keep the rest of the card structure.
vinyl_cover.spin: The disc rotation is a CSS `@keyframes spin{to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}` with `animation-play-state` driven by playback: the disc spins ONLY while the audio is PLAYING (`animation-play-state:running`, e.g. via a `.playing` class on the wrapper) and is PAUSED otherwise (`animation-play-state:paused`). Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` the spin is DISABLED (`animation:none`) — the disc is shown static. The spin state is wired in lockstep with the play/pause button and the first-gesture autostart, so the disc visibly spins iff the track is playing.
vinyl_cover.reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion:reduce removes the spin entirely (static disc); the player still works (audio + button).

signature_media_card.build: A SELF-HOSTED card placed at the TOP of the article, directly BELOW THE TITLE (in-flow as the opening content block, centered in the column — NOT a fixed corner widget): the cover art as a SPINNING VINYL DISC (circular, spins only while playing via animation-play-state; spin disabled under prefers-reduced-motion — see vinyl_cover) + an optional EYEBROW kind label ('Official anthem' / 'Film theme' / 'Signature track', uppercase letter-spaced --muted) + title + artist(s) + a one-line description (what it is / why it matters) + a single play/pause control bound to an `<audio>` whose `src` is a self-hosted file, beside a small status label. Surface = --surface, design_tokens radius/shadow/padding.
signature_media_card.eyebrow: A short uppercase, letter-spaced KIND label above the title (--muted) that tells the reader at a glance WHAT the track is — 'Official anthem', 'Film theme', 'Campaign jingle', 'Signature track' — so the card reads as a deliberate now-playing piece, not a stray audio widget. It states the track's kind, not a marketing line.
signature_media_card.autostart: Autostart on the reader's FIRST gesture anywhere on the page (browsers block bare autoplay): `addEventListener('pointerdown'/'keydown', startOnce, {once:true})` -> `audio.play()`, then reflect state in the play/pause button AND start the disc spin (add the `.playing` class). Keep it reader-controllable (pause/replay) and respect a muted preference; never blast at full volume — set a moderate `audio.volume`.
signature_media_card.scroll_to_start: ALSO offer scroll as a start affordance: bind the same one-time start handler to the passive scroll/wheel/touchmove events alongside the first click/tap/keydown, so the soundtrack can begin AS THE READER SCROLLS into the story. A pure scroll/wheel does NOT grant audio activation on its own, so gate on the `play()` promise — only mark started + remove all listeners on the resolved promise (and start the disc spin there), and keep listening (so the next real gesture starts it) on rejection. The status label reflects this ('Starts as you scroll'). The explicit play/pause button always remains; scroll-to-start is an additional affordance, never the only one.
signature_media_card.why_self_host: A Spotify/YouTube embed as the primary player fails the goal: non-logged-in listeners get only a ~30s preview, and neither autoplays from the start on a gesture. Self-host the actual track so the experience is complete and consistent.
signature_media_card.secondary_link: KEEP a 3rd-party embed or link, but ONLY as a secondary 'listen to the official version on Spotify/YouTube' affordance below the card — not the main player.
signature_media_card.license_note: An official track is usually copyrighted: a local build may self-host it, but it must clear the PUBLISH GATE (license / swap to a clean cue / accept-IP with awareness) before public hosting — see media_presentation license_posture. A license-clean classical RECORDING (verify the recording, not just the PD composition) is the always-available clean fallback.
signature_media_card.anti_pattern: Making a Spotify/YouTube embed the primary player; a silent 'cover + link' card the reader must leave the page to hear; a static square cover instead of the spinning vinyl disc; a disc that spins while paused or keeps spinning under reduced-motion.

scrollytelling: Sticky visual + scrolling steps; IntersectionObserver swaps/höighlights the visual per step; smooth CSS transitions; stacks on mobile.
before_after: Two layered images/maps with a draggable divider (clip-path or overflow); works on touch + mouse; labeled states.
guess_reveal: Ask the reader to predict (slider/choice) before revealing the real value with a short animation; maximizes a surprising finding.
data_table: For dense comparisons: sticky header, zebra/hover rows, right-aligned numerics, the winning cell highlighted with --accent; horizontally scrollable on mobile.
figure: Images in <figure> margin:2rem auto, rounded corners, <figcaption> centered in --muted. Note when an image is an illustration vs a real photo.
references_footer: Compact list (UI font, --muted) of data source + studies + tools, with links. A footer, not a bibliography page.
